item.content:encoded:
There are a couple possibilities that would let censoring make sense in-universe:

-Knowing what it is could make it worse. The Foundation knows more than one monster that gets deadlier the more it's victim knows about it.

-Knowing could cause morale problems. Maybe the beasts look like family members or the victims themselves. There are a lot of images that could get under a soldier's skin and shake them up, and knowing the specific shape of what may jump out at you may not help enough to be worth the tactical disadvantage of scared men.

-Knowing could reveal classified information. Maybe the monsters look like the O5 council, or world leaders that have been replaced by robots, or they are all the cherubs Foundation chemists tore the wings off to make amnestics. The Foundation has a lot of secrets they consider more important than staff lives, this may be one of them.

I'm not trying to convince you to change your vote. You (don't) like whatever you like.
Just wanted to point out that problematic expungement is not necessarily a plot hole.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It is different in a lot of ways, but one is the most important:
432 is an isolated object, something that is very easy to control and hide.

432 comes off as much, much more threatening, despite the fact that it's "controlled", especially if you read through the experiment logs. It's claustrophobic, darker, the screams may or may not be real, its purpose and construction is suspect, it's observable and recordable enough to incite curiosity, and its perceived safety leaves a looming threat that there may someday be a breach - and we don't know the consequences of such a breach. This one just killed some site staff, killing what little sense of looming dread it bothered to construct.

This could be any hedge maze. Anywhere, any one you ever go to, could hide this.

That "you could find this" attitude only incites fright if the concept isn't so damn predictable. Oh, I'd get lost in a murderous hedge maze? You'd bet people would join the site just thinking of the idea! :/

I mean, it hardly stands out in the Foundation universe as a unique it-could-happen-to-you. We have commercially farmed tomatoes that might kill you if you pun badly.

Hence, a nice jump in creep factor.

item.content:encoded:
This shows promise, but besides the already-mentioned blandness, I think a major problem with it is that it's too vague. Like, "The [REDACTED] radio [REDACTED] market." wouldn't make you think of anything, but "The [REDACTED] specimen proceeded to systematically take apart the radio and reassemble it into [REDACTED]. Due to [REDACTED] the nearby market at [REDACTED] evacuated and destroyed."

I think I've put across what I'm getting at- I don't seem to be very good with my words at the moment. But it otherwise does show promise. If/when you do start tightening it up, I would recommend elaborating on the 'monsters' before anything and making the capabilities of the 'maze' a bit more solid- it says that you can't go through the plants or jump over the hedges, but the censored parts just seem to come across as "You just can't, okay? Forget it." Even elaborating on the 'hidden entrance' would be welcome.

You still want to be vague, but not too vague.
